WITH filtered_budgets AS (
    SELECT 
        category,
        remaining,
        amount,
        spent
    FROM budget
    WHERE amount >= 75
),
category_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        category,
        AVG(remaining) as avg_remaining,
        SUM(amount - spent) as total_amount_minus_spent
    FROM filtered_budgets
    GROUP BY category
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_amount_minus_spent) as overall_avg
    FROM category_stats
)
SELECT 
    cs.category,
    cs.avg_remaining,
    cs.total_amount_minus_spent,
    cs.total_amount_minus_spent - oa.overall_avg as above_average
FROM category_stats cs
CROSS JOIN overall_average oa
WHERE cs.total_amount_minus_spent > oa.overall_avg

assumptions.assumption: NULL values in amount, spent, or remaining columns are handled per standard SQL semantics: aggregates (AVG, SUM) skip NULL values; arithmetic expressions (amount - spent) return NULL if either operand is NULL. This aligns with the request's phrase 'ignoring missing values'
